title: Check the SDK offline: types, route table, unit and contract tests, bundles
caption: Nothing to start: these commands use a fake fetch and never touch the network. Run them from the repository root. They are what CI runs for the SDK (plus the sdk-node22 job on Node.js 22.12.0).

steps.title: Build the generated API types once
steps.body: `pnpm --filter @velexis/api-types build` (typecheck, build and the contract/bundle tests read the built `@velexis/api-types`; Turborepo does this for you when you use `pnpm exec turbo run …`).

steps.title: Regenerate the route table and compare
steps.expect: No change to `src/internal/operations.js` or `test/contract/methods.generated.ts`. A diff means the OpenAPI document changed without regenerating: CI fails on it.

steps.title: Unit and contract tests
steps.body: `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test` (Vitest: `test/unit/**` and `test/contract/**`). One file: `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk exec vitest run test/unit/session-cookie.test.js`.
steps.expect: All green. The contract tests also prove: 129 methods equal the document's `x-sdk-method` set (parity), every `@throws` matches the operation's `x-error-codes`, `VERSION` equals `package.json`.

steps.title: Build the bundles and check the size
steps.expect: `dist/velexis-sdk.mjs`, `dist/velexis-sdk.iife.js`, `dist/types/*.d.ts` and the printed size, about 15.8 KB min+gzip of the 25 KB budget. Above 25 KB the build fails.

steps.title: Lint
steps.expect: No ESLint errors (the SDK never calls `console.*`).
